newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE reaches agreement to buy new London site.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE reaches agreement to buy new London site.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Monday it reached an agreement with Spitalfields Developments Limited to buy a site for developing a new open outcry trading floor and offices.

"Under the agreement LIFFE and SDL (Spitalfields Developments Limited) have agreed to enter into exclusive negotiations for the acquisition of the site and its development," LIFFE said in a statement.

LIFFE, one of the world's busiest derivatives exchanges, also said it had concluded terms with the City Corporation under which the City Corporation would reacquire the site if LIFFE decided not to proceed at any time prior to December 31, 2001.
"This agreement is made necessary by the huge growth in volumes in recent years," said LIFFE chairman Jack Wigglesworth in the statement.

Wigglesworth, who said 1996 had beaten all previous records for business, added the exchange was gearing up for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU). "We anticipate further growth in trading volumes as our EMU strategy brings more business to LIFFE," he said.
Philip Willoughby, chairman of the Corporation City Land Committee, said the agreement was positive for the London financial district, known as the City.
"It reinforces the City's position as Europe's premier financial centre," Willoughby said.
The statement did not disclose terms of the agreement.

A LIFFE spokesman said LIFFE had been looking for a site of up to 100,000 square feet, but he said he could not comment on the size of the site in the agreement. He said LIFFE had looked at six sites, including one at Canary Wharf.
SDL is owned by BICC Plc, SPP Real Estate (UK) and Costain Plc.

Spitalfields, famous for its covered market, is adjacent to the north-east of the City. Early in 1996, Dutch bank ABN AMRO said it would relocate all of its London operations to a new Spitalfields office building.
